summary: In Greek mythology, Eurymedon (Ancient Greek: Εὐρυμέδων, "ruling far and wide") was an Argonaut from Phlius, son of Dionysus and Ariadne and brother of Phlias — one of several minor figures who share the name.

sections.heading: Argonaut from Phlius
paragraphs: Hyginus names Eurymedon son of Liber (Dionysus) and Ariadne among the Argonauts, pairing him with the Phliasian contingent. He is brother of Phlias (Phliasus), the better-attested eponymous Argonaut of Phlius; both stand in the Peloponnesian roll of the Minyae.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (eurymedon-phlius) is the Phliasian Argonaut son of Dionysus and Ariadne. Distinct from many other Eurymedons: the Giant king father of Periboea; Agamemnon's and Nestor's squires in the Iliad; a son of Minos slain by Heracles on Paros; Cabiri and Theban gate-defenders; and a Titan or Giant said to have outraged Hera.
